prompt: Create a Stripe customer with the given email address and a metadata entry `plan` set to "pro". Return the new customer's id.

Create a Checkout Session in payment mode for one unit of the given price id, sending the buyer to https://example.com/ok on success and https://example.com/no if they cancel. Return the session's hosted URL.
Create a PaymentIntent for the given amount in USD, letting Stripe decide which payment methods to offer automatically. Return the client secret.
Subscribe the given customer to the given price and return the subscription id.
Verify a raw webhook payload against the signature header and the endpoint secret. If the resulting event is a completed Checkout Session, return that session's id; otherwise return null.
Collect the ids of every customer in the account, letting the SDK walk the pages for you rather than handling cursors by hand. Ask for 100 per page.
Retrieve a PaymentIntent by id and have Stripe return the full customer object alongside it rather than just the id. Return whatever the customer field holds.
Refund the given amount from the given PaymentIntent and return the refund id.
List the first five customers that belong to a connected account, given that account's id. Use the same client — do not build a second one.
Create a customer with the given email in a way that is safe to retry, so a repeated call with the same email cannot create a duplicate. Return the customer id.
Create a PaymentIntent for the given amount in USD. If Stripe rejects the card, return the decline code it gives you; rethrow anything else.
Create a draft invoice for the given customer, finalize it, and return the hosted invoice URL.
Build and export the Stripe client this project uses: pin it to the API version this installed SDK targets, give it a 30 second timeout and let it retry twice on network failure.
